title: Her window calls tabs_focus and daemon_restart, which athena.json never grants
body:
## Summary
Three buttons in Athena's own window (go to tab, retry engine, use engine) call Tauri commands that `apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/athena.json` does not grant, so in the real window each one is refused by the ACL.

## Description
The athena window is covered by `capabilities/athena.json` alone (ui.json names the `chrome` webview). It grants no `allow-tabs-focus` and no `allow-daemon-restart`, and its description says she is given no tabs_focus on purpose ('she reads what Main has open and never ... selects anything in it'). Yet `apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:387` wires `goToTab` to `useTabs.getState().focus` (tabs_focus, added by c0a9edb with the card's go-to-tab button at `apps/desktop/src/companion/views.tsx:340`), `apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:385` wires `retryEngine` to `useDaemon.getState().restart` and `:382` `useEngine` to `chooseFirstRunEngine`, which reaches `daemon_restart` through `apps/desktop/src/stores/daemon.ts:167`. `apps/desktop/src/stores/settings.ts:214` also asks `store_path` from her window (caught, harmless). The registry's ipc-contract/command-registration technique names exactly this: R - P per surface, 'registered but not granted', failing at runtime with a bare string. Fixing it is either widening her capability (policy-loosen, and for tabs_focus a reversal of the stated rule) or routing the act to Main by event; both are a call for the operator.

## Flow
- First run: her welcome offers an engine; press Use (data-act=use-engine) -> chooseFirstRunEngine -> ensureEngine -> daemon_restart -> refused by the ACL ('daemon_restart not allowed') -> reported as an engine error
- A card bound to another tab: press Go to tab (data-act=go-to-tab) -> tabs_focus -> refused
- Fix option A: add allow-tabs-focus and allow-daemon-restart to athena.json and amend its description (policy-loosen)
- Fix option B: her window emits to Main (as athenaOffer does with emitTo) and Main performs the focus or restart (no grant widens)

## Expected impact
8

## Evaluation
Claim: user - three buttons in her window stop failing
Before: 3 commands reachable from her window's handlers (tabs_focus, daemon_restart, store_path) are absent from athena.json's 22 grants; 0 tests check grants per window
After: unmeasured: needs the decision between widening the grant and routing through Main, then the real Tauri window to see the buttons work
Method: simulation - traced live.tsx:382-387 -> stores -> lib wrappers -> command names, and compared with athena.json; the per-window derivation was not built because the fix needs a policy call first, and the effect needs the real window (memory: the companion was never verified in it)
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:382 useEngine -> chooseFirstRunEngine (stores/settings.ts:160 ensureEngine)
apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:385 retryEngine -> useDaemon.restart -> stores/daemon.ts:167 daemonRestart -> "daemon_restart"
apps/desktop/src/companion/live.tsx:387 goToTab -> useTabs.focus -> "tabs_focus"
apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/athena.json permissions: no allow-tabs-focus, no allow-daemon-restart, no allow-store-path, no allow-captures-sweep
athena.json description: "It is given no tabs_create, tabs_close, tabs_focus, tabs_navigate or layout_*"
apps/desktop/src/athena.tsx:39-57 starts tabs, tools, daemon, settings, run, voice in her window

title: The captures cap is never held from her window: captures_sweep is refused there
body:
## Summary
Captures are taken in Athena's window, and each one is followed by a `captures_sweep` call that `capabilities/athena.json` does not grant, so the cap of README 3.5 holds only when Main starts.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/lib/hands.ts:127` sweeps after every capture `takeCapture` files, and `:151` once per window at `startHands`. The run store, which calls `takeCapture` (`apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:421`), lives only in her window (`apps/desktop/src/athena.tsx:45`), and `startTools` -> `startHands` runs there too (`apps/desktop/src/athena.tsx:39`). Her capability has no `allow-captures-sweep`, so every one of those sweeps is refused and only logged (`hands.ts:95`). Main (`apps/desktop/src/console/root.tsx:30`) sweeps once at its own start. Between launches of Main the `captures` table grows past its declared cap. A fix that widens no access: Rust sweeps inside the capture path after it files a row (src-tauri/src/capture.rs or hands.rs), so no webview needs the command; the alternative is granting it to her window.

## Flow
- her window: a request -> takeCapture -> hands_call page_screenshot files a row -> sweepCaptures -> captures_sweep -> ACL refusal -> console.error
- repeat for every request until Main is restarted; the table only shrinks at Main's startHands
- fix: Rust calls Store::captures_sweep(CAPTURES_CAP_BYTES) after it inserts a capture; the panel's sweep becomes redundant

## Expected impact
6

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the captures table stays under its cap while she works
Before: 0 of the sweeps her window asks for are granted (athena.json has no allow-captures-sweep)
After: unmeasured: needs the Rust change in another context (desktop-shell-rust) and a cargo test
Method: simulation - traced takeCapture -> sweepCaptures -> captures_sweep in her window against athena.json's grants; the probe needs src-tauri, outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/lib/hands.ts:94 capturesSweep() after a filed capture
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:421 capture: takeCapture (run store is her window's: athena.tsx:45)
apps/desktop/src/athena.tsx:39 startTools() -> stores/tools.ts:137 startHands()
apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/athena.json: no allow-captures-sweep
apps/desktop/src-tauri/capabilities/ui.json: allow-captures-sweep (chrome webview only)
instrument: a cargo test in src-tauri that files captures past CAPTURES_CAP_BYTES through the page_screenshot path and asserts the table is back under the cap; or the per-window grant check from the commands parity test

title: isReadCall reads a page's tabs_read flags for a call that runs the shell's hand
body:
## Summary
`apps/desktop/src/lib/execute.ts:57` looks a bare name up in the page's tools before the hands, so for `tabs_read` it reads the page's flags although the call always runs the shell's hand (ADR 0105).

## Description
withHands drops a page's `tabs_read` and isHandCall always routes it to the shell (`apps/desktop/src/lib/hands.ts:168,176`); this round made toolRows agree (29443fb). `isReadCall` is the third rendering and still lets the page's tool win, so whether a timed-out tabs_read is `timeout` or `outcome_unknown` (ADR 0101) depends on flags a page wrote for a tool that never runs. The fix is one line: skip page tools named TABS_READ, or look the name up in withHands(pageTools).

## Flow
- page registers tabs_read with reversible:false
- the model calls tabs_read; the shell's hand runs and times out
- settleHostCall -> isReadCall finds the page's tool -> not a read -> outcome_unknown, and the rest of the exchange is tightened as if a write may have run

## Expected impact
3

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one tabs_read rule in all three places
Before: 2 of 3 sites (withHands, isHandCall) apply the reservation; isReadCall does not
After: 3 of 3, by the instrument named
Method: simulation - read execute.ts:56-61 against hands.ts:167-177; execute.ts is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a case in src/lib/execute.test.ts: page registers tabs_read with write flags, the hand is a read; isReadCall('tabs_read', pageTools) must read the hand

title: Every refused answer tells the person to focus the app, even when that cannot help
body:
## Summary
`refusalSentence` (`apps/desktop/src/companion/plain.ts:46`) appends 'Focus the app this decision is about and try again.' to every reason, including expired, declined, spent and not-ready, where focusing changes nothing.

## Description
The sentence under a card's buttons is `That answer was refused: <clause>. Focus the app this decision is about and try again.` The remedy is right for foreign_origin (the one it was written for) and plausibly no_manifest; for 'it ran out of time', 'it was already declined', 'that decision is no longer waiting', 'that approval was already used once', 'Athena is still starting' and 'Athena did not answer' it sends the person to do something that cannot work, and they will press again into the same refusal. `plainFailure` already gives each reason its own remedy; `refusalSentence` should too. plain.ts was granted to this round only for the approval_spent item.

## Flow
- a card expires while the person reads it; they press Approve
- the daemon refuses expired -> refusalSentence -> '...it ran out of time. Focus the app this decision is about and try again.'
- they focus the app and press again -> the same refusal
- fix: a remedy per reason family, pinned by the instrument

## Expected impact
5

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the remedy under a refused answer is one that can work
Before: the focus remedy is appended for all 14 codes plainReason names; it can change the outcome for 3 (foreign_origin, no_manifest, manifest_invalid) and for none of the other 11
After: 14 of 14 by the instrument named
Method: simulation - read plain.ts:11-46 for each reason the gate returns; plain.ts is outside this round's write set beyond its assigned item
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/companion/plain.ts:46 return `That answer was refused: ${plainReason(reason)}. Focus the app this decision is about and try again.`;
apps/desktop/src/stores/run.ts:1433 const sentence = local ?? (off ? switchedOffSentence() : refusalSentence(reason));
instrument: a plain.test.ts case: for each policy refusal, the remedy clause is one that can change the outcome (focus only for foreign_origin / no_manifest / foreign_token; 'ask again' for expired, unknown_ref, user_denied, approval_spent, validator_failed; 'in a moment' for not_ready, unreachable)

title: athena_snap_to is registered and granted to two windows, and nothing calls it
body:
## Summary
`athena_snap_to` (docking her window by name) is declared in build.rs, registered in lib.rs and granted in ui.json and athena.json, but no code in the tree invokes it; it is attack and maintenance surface with no witness.

## Description
Added in 265a41d ('can dock and open Main') with no TS caller then or since. The commands parity test landed this round (de1369c) carries it as the one named loan in UNINVOKED. Either a surface adopts it (a dock menu, a keyboard path to dock, which would also give the drag-only docking an accessible alternative) or it is removed from the four lists and companion.rs (`snap_to` is used only by it). Which one is a product call.

## Flow
- git grep athena_snap_to -> build.rs:69, lib.rs:219, companion.rs:878, capabilities ui.json and athena.json; 0 hits in apps/desktop/src
- option A: wire a dock-by-name action in her window (keyboard alternative to dragging)
- option B: delete the command, its two grants and companion::snap_to, and drop the loan from commands.test.ts

## Expected impact
4

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no registered command without a caller
Before: 1 of 28 registered commands has 0 callers (commands.test.ts UNINVOKED)
After: 0 of 28 under either option
Method: gate - commands.test.ts derives R - I from the files; the choice between the arms is a direction
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
$ git grep -n athena_snap_to
apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs:69
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/companion.rs:878
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:219
(capabilities) ui.json allow-athena-snap-to, athena.json allow-athena-snap-to
0 matches under apps/desktop/src
